proof_skeleton_nl: For each genus level h, convert a tuple k in K_{m,h} into the numerical semigroup S(k) whose elements in residue class r modulo m begin at m k_r + r, and convert a multiplicity-m numerical semigroup S back to its Apery/Kunz tuple. Lemmas L1-L4 show that these two constructions are inverse bijections for h = g, and the same lemmas instantiated with h = g+1 give inverse bijections for h = g+1. Lemma L5 gives the finite cardinality inequality |NS_{m,g}| <= |NS_{m,g+1}| on the semigroup side. Lemma L6 then produces an injective map J from NS_{m,g} to NS_{m,g+1}. Finally, conjugate J by the two bijections: Phi_{m,g} = B_{g+1} o J o A_g. This composite is an injective function from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}, which is exactly the theorem.

steps.derives: Define A_g : K_{m,g} -> NS_{m,g} by sending a tuple k to the set S(k) = {0} union {q m : q in N, q >= 1} union {q m + r : r in {1,...,m-1}, q in N, q >= k_r}. By L1, for every k in K_{m,g}, the set S(k) is a numerical semigroup of multiplicity m and genus g, so A_g is well-defined.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct instantiation of L1 with the tuple k and the explicit definition of A_g(k).

steps.derives: Define B_g : NS_{m,g} -> K_{m,g} by sending a numerical semigroup S to its tuple of Apery/Kunz coordinates ((w_1-1)/m, ..., (w_{m-1}-(m-1))/m), where w_r is the least element of S congruent to r modulo m. By L2, for every S in NS_{m,g}, this tuple lies in K_{m,g}, so B_g is well-defined.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct instantiation of L2 with the numerical semigroup S and the explicit coordinate extraction.

steps.derives: For every k in K_{m,g}, one has B_g(A_g(k)) = k.
steps.trivial_justification: After unfolding A_g and B_g, this is exactly the statement of L3.

steps.derives: For every S in NS_{m,g}, one has A_g(B_g(S)) = S.
steps.trivial_justification: After unfolding A_g and B_g, this is exactly the statement of L4.

steps.derives: The maps A_g and B_g are inverse bijections between K_{m,g} and NS_{m,g}.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A3 gives B_g o A_g = id on K_{m,g}, so A_g is injective and B_g is surjective. Step A4 gives A_g o B_g = id on NS_{m,g}, so B_g is injective and A_g is surjective. Therefore both maps are bijections and each is the inverse of the other.

steps.derives: Define A_{g+1} : K_{m,g+1} -> NS_{m,g+1} by the same residue-wise formula k |-> S(k). By L1 with g replaced by g+1, this map is well-defined.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the same direct application of L1 as in A1, now with parameter g+1.

steps.derives: Define B_{g+1} : NS_{m,g+1} -> K_{m,g+1} by the same Apery/Kunz coordinate formula S |-> ((w_1-1)/m, ..., (w_{m-1}-(m-1))/m). By L2 with g replaced by g+1, this map is well-defined.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the same direct application of L2 as in A2, now with parameter g+1.

steps.derives: The maps A_{g+1} and B_{g+1} are inverse bijections between K_{m,g+1} and NS_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: Instantiating L3 with g replaced by g+1 gives B_{g+1}(A_{g+1}(k)) = k for every k in K_{m,g+1}. Instantiating L4 with g replaced by g+1 gives A_{g+1}(B_{g+1}(S)) = S for every S in NS_{m,g+1}. As in A5, the two-sided inverse identities imply that A_{g+1} and B_{g+1} are bijections and inverses of each other.

steps.derives: The sets NS_{m,g} and NS_{m,g+1} are finite and satisfy |NS_{m,g}| <= |NS_{m,g+1}|.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L5.

steps.derives: There exists an injective function J : NS_{m,g} -> NS_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L6 to the finite sets A = NS_{m,g} and B = NS_{m,g+1} using the finiteness and cardinality inequality obtained in A9.

steps.derives: There exists an injective function Phi_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: Define Phi_{m,g} = B_{g+1} o J o A_g. By A5, A_g is a bijection from K_{m,g} onto NS_{m,g}. By A10, J is an injective function from NS_{m,g} to NS_{m,g+1}. By A8, B_{g+1} is a bijection from NS_{m,g+1} onto K_{m,g+1}. Therefore the composite Phi_{m,g} is a well-defined function K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}. Since bijections are injective and the composition of injective maps is injective, Phi_{m,g} is injective. Hence an injective function from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1} exists, exactly as required.
